target.title: security(audit): warn on plugin load paths and SecretRef env fallback
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes two operator visibility gaps in OpenClaw security posture checks:

1. **`plugins.load.paths` trust-boundary risk** — Operators can point `plugins.load.paths` at arbitrary local directories, but `openclaw security audit` did not evaluate those configured paths for filesystem risk (world-writable paths, missing entries, bundled aliases, synced folders) before runtime plugin load.
2. **SecretRef env fallback visibility** — Runtime secret resolution already emits diagnostics when a configured SecretRef fails and provider env credentials are used instead, but `openclaw security audit` and doctor did not surface that boundary drift.

## Why This Change Was Made

Added a config-layer plugin load path collector that reuses existing discovery and doctor bundled-path helpers, then maps results to structured security audit findings (`plugins.load_paths.*`). Added a shared secrets diagnostic helper (`collectSecretRefEnvFallbackDiagnostics`) used by both security audit (`secrets.ref_env_fallback_used`) and a new doctor health check (`core/doctor/secretref-env-fallback`). Deep skill code-safety scan retains `includeArchived: true`.

## User Impact

* Operators running `openclaw security audit` now get early warnings when `plugins.load.paths` points at risky or missing locations, and when configured SecretRefs silently fall back to env credentials.
* `openclaw doctor` now emits structured warnings for SecretRef env fallback cases that previously only appeared in runtime/gateway logs.
* No config schema, runtime enforcement, or secret resolution behavior changes.

## Evidence

```bash
node scripts/run-vitest.mjs run \
  src/security/audit-plugin-load-paths.test.ts \
  src/security/audit-secretref-env-fallback.test.ts \
  src/secrets/secretref-env-fallback-diagnostics.test.ts \
  --reporter=verbose
```

## Real behavior proof

- **Behavior or issue addressed:** Security audit and doctor did not surface risky `plugins.load.paths` entries or SecretRef env-fallback boundary drift.
- **Real environment tested:** macOS (Darwin arm64), Node.js v22.22.0, local source checkout on branch `codex/audit-load-paths-secretref-fallback` (single commit on latest `main`).
- **Exact steps or command run after this patch:**
  1. `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs run src/security/audit-plugin-load-paths.test.ts src/security/audit-secretref-env-fallback.test.ts src/secrets/secretref-env-fallback-diagnostics.test.ts --reporter=verbose`
  2. Programmatic doctor health-check detect via production `CORE_HEALTH_CHECKS` entry `core/doctor/secretref-env-fallback` (same code path as `openclaw doctor` Gateway auth contribution)
- **Evidence after fix:**

```text
 ✓ flags world-writable configured plugin load paths
 ✓ flags missing configured plugin load paths
 ✓ maps shared diagnostics to a security audit finding
 ✓ flags gateway token SecretRef env fallback
 ✓ skips gateway token fallback when auth mode is password

 Test Files  3 passed (3)
      Tests  8 passed (8)

[warning] core/doctor/secretref-env-fallback: gateway.auth.token SecretRef could not be resolved; runtime is using OPENCLAW_GATEWAY_TOKEN env fallback.
doctor findings: 1
```

- **Observed result after fix:** Audit collectors emit `plugins.load_paths.*` and `secrets.ref_env_fallback_used`; the doctor health check `core/doctor/secretref-env-fallback` (wired under `doctor:gateway-auth`) surfaces the same shared diagnostic as a warning.
- **What was not tested:** Live gateway startup with real SecretRef providers; no committed `scripts/proof-*.mjs` helpers.

## AI-assisted disclosure

- AI-assisted (Cursor agent)
- Human-directed scope and review of audit/doctor wiring
